The talks aim to reach a compromise formula allowing the issue to be deferred to after 30 September and preventing the dispute over restricting weapons to state control from becoming a confrontation between the factions and Iraqi forces.
This comes as the government confirms that dialogue with the factions is proceeding regularly and that the dispute is focused primarily on mechanisms for implementing the process of restricting weapons.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has less than 40 days left to complete "restricting weapons to the hands of the state", as the deadline granted to the factions expires on 30 September.
But this date may not be final, particularly as some factions have refused to cooperate with the Iraqi state on the matter.
"The direction being proposed within the Coordination Framework is not to cancel the decision to restrict weapons to the hands of the state but to extend the timeframe allocated for negotiations and implementation, allowing for a final agreement to be reached on mechanisms for handing over weapons," the sources said.
"This would take into account the demand of the factions opposed to the move that any step in this direction be preceded by the complete withdrawal of US and international coalition forces from Iraqi territory, scheduled for 30 Sept," they said.
According to the sources, "Nouri al-Maliki, leader of the State of Law Coalition, has joined this process alongside Badr Organisation leader Hadi al-Amiri and Hikma Movement leader Ammar al-Hakim."
"A proposal is now being discussed within the Coordination Framework to avoid any escalation measures after the specified deadline and instead work to use the period following the US withdrawal to complete understandings with the factions, particularly Hezbollah Brigades, al-Nujaba Movement and Sayyid al-Shuhada Brigades, which remain among the main forces opposed to the immediate handover of weapons," the sources added.
The sources further noted that unannounced talks are still taking place between the negotiating committee formed by the Coordination Framework and the factions on one side and the government on the other.
The talks seek to reach a final agreement on implementing the decision to restrict weapons to the hands of the state and postpone the deadline beyond 30 Sept.
The sources stressed these proposals are being discussed during meetings to prevent any anticipated serious security escalation and said a final plan will be reached in the coming days.
Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi's statements last Friday, 21 August, are particularly significant in this context after he explained that 30 Sept. is the date for the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq, not "the final deadline for the factions to restrict their weapons".
He also confirmed that dialogue with the factions is progressing and that the current dispute concerns mechanisms.
Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi stressed that his government has no intention of engaging in a military confrontation with the factions and that work is continuing to establish mechanisms for handing over weapons.
These moves come as political and security concerns grow that the expiry of the deadline without an agreement could put the government before a highly sensitive test.
It would either have to implement its decision through security measures that could lead to a confrontation with factions possessing military capabilities and political influence or accept an extension of negotiations, which could be interpreted politically as a retreat from the previous timeframe.
For this reason, the mediation led by Coordination Framework leaders appears primarily aimed at managing the period after the end of September without a security explosion while maintaining the principle of restricting weapons to the hands of the state as the final basis for a settlement.
Ali al-Yaseri, a member of the Coordination Framework, told The New Arab, "Postponing the deadline for restricting weapons to the hands of the state beyond next Sept. 30 is an option on the table and under discussion, and there is nothing to prevent extending the period if that serves Iraq's higher interests and ensures the decision is implemented properly without entering into any security escalation."
"30 Sept. is not a constitutional date or one set by law, but rather a political and security deadline adopted as part of the process of addressing the issue of weapons and the military presence of the international coalition," al-Yaseri said. "Therefore, postponing it for a limited period does not mean retreating from or cancelling the decision to restrict weapons to the hands of the state."
"Dialogue between the parties concerned with this issue is ongoing and continuous, and there is serious discussion about the possibility of granting an additional period that could extend to one or two months," he added. "This is particularly the case if there are genuine intentions among the factions concerned to implement the state's decision according to mechanisms and guarantees agreed in advance."
He confirmed that "the postponement, if adopted, will be linked to several issues, foremost among them completing the withdrawal of international coalition forces from Iraqi territory and agreeing on a clear mechanism for handing over weapons."
"This also includes determining the political, security and legal guarantees accompanying the implementation process in a way that prevents a vacuum or security tensions," he said.
Al-Yaseri stressed that "the aim of any possible extension is not to give the factions an open-ended deadline but to provide enough time to finalise the agreement and reach a practical implementation of the decision to restrict weapons to the hands of the state, away from any confrontation or clash that could have serious repercussions for the overall political and security situation in Iraq."
"The priority now is to make the dialogue successful and reach an understanding that preserves the state's authority and sovereignty while at the same time preventing a move towards escalation options. Therefore, all options relating to the timing and mechanisms of implementation remain under consideration and discussion among the parties concerned," he concluded.
If the situation moves towards postponing the 30 Sept. deadline, the weapons issue in Iraq will have entered a different negotiating phase whose main focus will be finding a settlement that postpones the moment of resolution without abandoning the principle of restricting weapons to the hands of the state.
In contrast, strategic affairs expert Hussein al-Asaad told TNA, "Care must be taken to ensure that any government retreat from the decision to restrict weapons to the hands of the state, or an extension of the implementation deadline without a clear process and defined timeframe, does not expose Iraq to major political and security repercussions."
"This is particularly important amid intensive international and US monitoring of this issue. The weapons issue is no longer purely an internal matter but has become linked to Iraq's image and its relations with Washington and the international community," he said.
Al-Asaad further explained that "the government must distinguish between postponing implementation for technical and political reasons linked to finalising understandings and retreating from the decision itself, because the two are entirely different."
"Any postponement must be announced as part of a clear and specific plan that includes stages, implementation mechanisms and guarantees so that it is not understood externally as the government's inability to enforce the state's decision," he added.
"The United States is closely monitoring this issue, as are other international parties, because the issue of weapons outside state institutions is directly linked to the level of stability and Iraqi sovereignty, the government's ability to control the territory and airspace, and its ability to prevent Iraq from being used as an arena for settling regional conflicts."
"The problem does not lie in holding dialogue with the factions or giving them additional time to implement the decision, as this process may be necessary to avoid a confrontation. Rather, the problem lies in the postponement turning into an open-ended policy without tangible results," al-Asaad further noted.
He warned that "this would weaken the government's position internally and externally and could give the impression that the decision to restrict weapons is reversible under pressure from armed groups.
"Iraq is facing a real test of state sovereignty. Therefore, any settlement should preserve the essence of the decision, which is that weapons and military decisions be placed within state institutions, while allowing for agreement on the stages, timing and guarantees of implementation demanded by some factions," he opined.
Al-Asaad continued, "A complete retreat from the decision could open the door to greater US and international pressure, particularly if armed groups possessing missile and drone capabilities remain outside state control."
"The government's success in managing this issue will not be measured only by its ability to avoid confrontation but also by its ability to reach an outcome that preserves the state's authority and sovereignty. Temporary de-escalation without a fundamental solution may postpone the crisis without ending it, while any ill-considered retreat from the decision to restrict weapons would be politically and security-wise costly for Iraq," he said.
For weeks, the Iraqi government has faced renewed escalation from the most influential factions closest to Tehran, most notably Hezbollah Brigades, al-Nujaba, Ansar Allah al-Awfiya and Sayyid al-Shuhada Brigades.
The factions have announced their refusal to hand over their weapons and considered the issue "not open to discussion".
This has coincided with a clear shift in the positions of other factions and groups following the visit to Baghdad two weeks ago by Ismail Qaani, commander of Iran's Quds Force, as well as the visit by Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf this week.
The visits came to strengthen the position of Iraqi factions that have begun to feel a real threat as a result of the judicial and government pressure in the country.

Bird flu is spreading. Your backyard feeder could make it worse
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:49:08 UTC
21:49:08 KST

Bird flu is spreading. Your backyard feeder could make it worse
- Date:
- August 24, 2026
- Source:
- The Conversation
- Summary:
- Backyard bird feeders could become unexpected hotspots for H5N1 as Australia’s bird flu outbreak spreads, bringing species together in ways that rarely occur naturally. Experts say stopping feeding is safest, while smaller amounts of food, no hand-feeding, and careful cleaning can reduce the danger.
- Share:
Backyard bird feeding is one of our country’s most popular pastimes. Research reveals about half of Australian households feed wild birds, with many people doing so daily.
However, this practice could act as a superspreader event – where a disease infects an unusually high number of people or animals – of the H5N1 virus. This deadly strain of bird flu has already decimated wild bird and mammal populations worldwide. It is now spreading across Australia, most recently killing more than 1,000 crested terns and a long-nosed fur seal, the first detection in a mainland mammal.
Although many Australians feed wild birds, the practice is controversial. This is mainly due to concerns about people offering unsuitable foods and birds becoming dependent on humans.
So why is backyard bird feeding such a problem when it comes to bird flu? And can we do it safely?
Not just a hobby
People feed wild birds for various reasons, including to provide food during tough times or simply enjoy their presence. Most care deeply about their avian companions and believe feeding them is helpful.
However, they may not realize the danger this creates for the birds they love.
Feeding wild birds heightens the risk of disease transmission at feeding locations. When we offer supplementary food, such as seeds or meat scraps, this attracts birds of many different species in a combination and number that would not happen in nature. They may carry deadly diseases, such as the H5N1 virus, and potentially spread them to other birds.
This can create a transmission hotspot right on our back deck. And catching bird flu can push our most threatened species, such as the orange-bellied parrot, to the brink of extinction.
The fatal effects of H5N1 are not only contained to birds. Scavenger animals such as possums, red foxes and crows can be exposed to the virus while devouring the carcasses of infected birds. Humans in close contact with infected wildlife, such as wildlife carers and veterinarians, can contract H5N1. However, human infection is rare and typically only causes mild symptoms.
Stopping the spread
Backyard bird feeding may seem like a harmless hobby. But given how many people do it, and the risks it poses to both birds and people, bird feeding activities could lead to many more wildlife deaths.
So if you feed birds in your backyard, how can you do so safely?
The most effective strategy is to stop feeding birds altogether. If you don’t offer food to wild birds, they will be less likely to congregate in your backyard or garden. And they will be fine without your help. Our previous research found most birds that visit feeders obtain most of their nutrition from natural sources, such as insects and worms. So the food we provide is a snack, not an essential meal.
But if you do continue feeding wild birds, here are three precautions to take:
Offer less food
Having feeders full of seeds and leftover meat will attract more birds. So to discourage them from congregating, simply provide less food. Much like COVID-era social distancing rules, this will lower the risk of H5N1 transmission by keeping birds separate.
Avoid hand-feeding
Having a bird swoop down to snatch food from your hand is one of the most intimate interactions we can have with wildlife. But in the era of bird flu, this must stop. While humans are unlikely to contract H5N1, close physical contact with birds through hand-feeding is simply not worth the risk.
Keep everything clean
If you keep feeding wild birds, it’s vital to regularly clean all feeding surfaces and equipment using domestic bleach. If you’re not prepared to do this, you shouldn’t be feeding them at all.
Backyard bird feeding could worsen Australia’s current H5N1 crisis. Indeed, your avian visitors may complain if you give them fewer tasty treats or stop feeding them altogether. But these measures will protect both you and them from this deadly disease.
Please do not touch sick or dead birds or marine mammals. Record the location, take photographs from a safe distance, keep pets away and report the sighting to the Emergency Animal Disease Hotline on 1800 675 888 (Australia).
Story Source:
Materials provided by The Conversation. Original written by Darryl Jones, Professor Emeritus, Centre for Planetary Health and Food Security, Griffith University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Gov’t board holds first meeting on PKK disarmament
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:49:00 UTC
21:49:00 KST

A panel established under legislation forming the legal framework for what the government calls the “terror-free Türkiye” initiative held its first meeting on Aug. 24 to oversee PKK’s disarmament and disso-lution process.
The Monitoring and Evaluation Board met under the chairmanship of Vice President Cevdet Yılmaz, with senior government officials attending, including Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, Defense Minister Yaşar Güler, Interior Minister Mustafa Çiftçi and Justice Minister Akın Gürlek.
National Intelligence Organization (MİT) chief İbrahim Kalın and National Security Council (MGK) head Okay Memiş were also present.
The meeting was expected to assess developments in PKK’s disarmament process and establish subcommittees to monitor and evaluate the implementation of the initiative.
The board was established under the Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Integration, which was approved by parliament on Aug. 10 and subsequently published in the Official Gazette.
The 12-article law passed with 467 votes in favor, 87 against and seven abstentions. It is intended to provide the legal framework for the government’s new initiative to end the decadeslong conflict with PKK.
Yılmaz said on Aug. 19 that the board would discuss its working procedures and principles during its first meeting, as well as the formation of subcommittees based on the needs of the disarmament and dissolution process.
Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) lawmaker Pervin Buldan, a prominent figure in the process, previously said jailed PKK leader Abdullah Öcalan would take part in a planned subcommittee overseeing the process.
Buldan said the proposed subcommittee would be called the “Disarmament and Politicization” committee and that Öcalan would participate in it and help coordinate developments.
The government had not confirmed Buldan’s remarks or provided details on how Öcalan could participate in the board’s work as of the Aug. 24 meeting.
According to the reports, another subcommittee is set to address judicial issues concerning PKK members who will apply for the postponement of the execution of their sentences. The decision over the postponement will be made by the judges in accordance with individual dossiers.
PKK announced in June 2025 that it would disband and end its armed campaign after Öcalan’s call on the organization. It is designated as a terror group by Türkiye, the United States and the European Union.

Tainan court detains three suspects over Annan District explosion
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:48:29 UTC
21:48:29 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — The Tainan District Prosecutors Office on Monday secured court approval to detain three suspects over a fire and explosion in Annan District that injured 15 people and affected more than 100 households.
CNA reported that the suspects are a local borough chief surnamed Cheng (鄭) and two men surnamed Yang (楊) and Kung (龔). Prosecutors said the three are suspected of offenses against public safety and violations of the Waste Disposal Act.
Prosecutors said there was a risk that the three suspects could destroy evidence or coordinate their statements. They also said Yang posed a flight risk and asked the Tainan District Court to detain the three and bar them from receiving visitors or communicating with people outside the detention center.
The court approved the requests after questioning the suspects. It said there was sufficient evidence to suspect the three of violating the Waste Disposal Act and reason to believe they could destroy evidence or coordinate their statements.
The court also found that Yang posed a flight risk. It said detention was necessary because the case involved multiple injuries and extensive property damage, per FTV News.
The fire broke out early Saturday at an open lot on Haidian Road in Annan District. A powerful explosion occurred while firefighters were putting out the blaze because the burning material contained magnesium-aluminum compounds.
The explosion injured 15 people, including three firefighters. Eleven homes were severely damaged, while another 102 households were also affected, per Liberty Times.
Investigators are trying to determine where the waste containing magnesium-aluminum compounds came from and why it was stored at the site. Prosecutors and police are continuing to investigate the case.

Breadcrumb
Mark Ruffalo slams 'dishonest' antisemitism claims as pro-Israel groups call for boycott
Mark Ruffalo has condemned "fundamentally dishonest" accusations of antisemitism against him made by pro-Israel advocacy groups, which are pushing to cancel the A-list actor over his criticisms of the billionaire Ellison family and its support for Israel's genocidal war in Gaza.
The Oscar-nominated actor, who has been among the most outspoken Hollywood figures against Israel's assault on Gaza, is also campaigning against Paramount Skydance's attempted takeover of Warner Bros Discovery, a merger which would create one of the largest media conglomerates in history.
In a statement on social media on Friday, Ruffalo discussed the links between David Ellison's Paramount Skydance and the software giant Oracle owned by his father Larry Ellison, whose technology is deeply embedded within the Israeli military.
Oracle has worked closely with Israeli military and security agencies for decades and its owners and executives are vocal supporters of the Israeli government.
The actor reshared a video of Oracle executive Safra Catz revealing the company had provided "really profoundly scary technology" to the Israeli military following the 7 October 2023 Hamas attack.
The clip accused Oracle of being "complicit in war crimes and crimes against humanity - including apartheid and genocide against Palestinians".
"These ‘really profoundly scary technologies’ will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you," Ruffalo wrote on Instagram.
"From one of the biggest tech companies in the world. Powering some of the most destructive and inhuman forces in the world. Why has Trump pushed this illegal merger through?" he continued.
He called on his followers to oppose the $111 billion merger, which he said would be "catastrophic" for the film industry.
Pro-Israel groups attack Ruffalo
His criticism of the Ellisons' ties to Israel has provoked accusations of antisemitism from the company as well as pro-Israel organisations such as the Anti-Defamation League and the Simon Wiesenthal Centre.
In a statement to The Wrap, a Paramount spokesperson accused Ruffalo of "invoking antisemitic tropes".
"Words like 'genocide' and 'apartheid,' applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong – they’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe," they said.
Creative Community for Peace, an organisation established to promote Israel's interests in the US entertainment industry, demanded a boycott of Ruffalo, who he claimed had used "extremist and antisemitic messaging".
The Anti-Defamation League's Jonathan Greenblatt described Ruffalo's statement "cynical and sickening" while Jim Berk, the CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Centre, called it "a textbook case of obsession and demonisation" of Jews.
In a viral post on Saturday, Ruffalo hit back at accusations, calling them "appalling and fundamentally dishonest".
"Criticising the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract, or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticising Jewish people. This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel," he wrote on X.
Ruffalo, whose latest Spiderman film is close to breaking box office records, has been consistently outspoken against Israel's genocide in Gaza and vocally supportive of Palestinian rights.
He was among almost 4,000 actors and film professionals who last year announced a boycott of Israel's entertainment industry, which they said was "implicated in genocide and apartheid against the Palestinian people".
Ruffalo also renewed calls for lawmakers to block the Paramount-Warner Bros merger, which he said would have "real consequences for the entire country".
"Scrutinising the Ellisons, including Oracle’s business built on data, surveillance technology and government contracts, and the serious threat to editorial freedom and the loss of a livelihood for thousands of families, is fair and necessary," he said.
"The $111 billion deal would hand one family control over CNN, HBO and Warner Bros., backed in part by foreign money whose influence on editorial decisions has never been fully explained to the public," he added.
Should it go ahead, the Paramount-Warner Bros deal would create one of the largest media conglomerates in the country, bringing together two of the world's largest film studios, as well as CBS, CNN and HBO. Larry Ellison also controls the US operations of social media giant TikTok, which has since clamped down on pro-Palestinian sentiment on the platform.
To complete the deal, Paramount-Skydance will need to overcome opposition from a dozen California attorneys, who have filed an antitrust suit against the company.
If it does not close by 30 September, Paramount Skydance will be forced to pay $7 million a day in fees to Warner Bros shareholders due to the delay.

NEW DELHI: Trying to accelerate the adoption of piped gas for cooking and industrial purposes, the Centre has asked states and Union Territories to provide district-level administrative support and appoint nodal officers to coordinate with gas distributors and oil marketing companies to expand the network.Govt has also directed authorised city gas distribution companies and public sector oil marketing companies to establish PNG coordination committees to identify eligible housing societies and households and conduct outreach camps to accelerate piped gas connections.In a letter to state chief secretaries, petroleum secretary Neeraj Mittal said PNG was crucial for India’s energy transition and could help reduce dependence on cooking gas cylinders.“PNG brings a safer, cleaner and more efficient cooking fuel, playing a critical role in advancing the country’s energy transition objectives. Govt is also trying to prevent households from retaining both LPG and PNG connections in areas where piped gas is available.

Could you give more details about the two meetings?
Lin Jian: The Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism is a new mechanism established between China and Indonesia. It provides vital institutional support for deepening bilateral cooperation across the “five pillars” under new circumstances. Foreign Minister Wang Yi and his Indonesian counterpart held a successful first conference. They spoke highly of the progress in cooperation across various fields, and agreed to deepen the alignment of development strategies and launch the formulation of a new five-year action plan for bilateral ties. The two sides agreed to set more ambitious bilateral trade targets and vigorously expand cooperation in new-quality productive forces such as artificial intelligence. The China-Indonesia Joint Foreign and Defense Dialogue is the first ministerial-level “2+2” mechanism China has established globally, and this marks the second meeting of the mechanism. The two sides agreed on the need to coordinate the two major tasks of development and security, foster a sense of security partnership, support each other’s core interests, jointly oppose external interference, and strive for greater progress in political security and defense cooperation. Both will safeguard the overall momentum of regional cooperation and maintain peace and stability in the South China Sea, strengthen policy coordination on multilateral platforms, oppose unilateral bullying and power politics, and safeguard international fairness, justice and the legitimate rights and interests of developing countries.
The world is currently at a crossroads between unity and division, and between cooperation and confrontation. As major developing countries and key members of the Global South, China and Indonesia’s efforts to strengthen strategic coordination and deepen solidarity and cooperation bears great significance far beyond the bilateral dimension. The success of China-Indonesia cooperation is also a success for the Global South. Guided by the strategic common understandings reached by the two heads of state, China stands ready to work with Indonesia to effectively translate consensus from the mechanism meetings into outcomes, expand and deepen all-round strategic cooperation, address risks and challenges, bolster respective modernization, and contribute more to stability and prosperity in the region and beyond.
China-Arab TV: King Abdullah II of Jordan is visiting China. We notice that an increasing number of leaders of Arab nations have visited China. China’s influence is on the rise, and China is playing an increasingly important role in the Arab world. What are the outcomes of King Abdullah II’s visit to China? What’s China’s expectation for China-Arab cooperation in the next couple of years?
Lin Jian: China and Jordan enjoy traditional friendship. Under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and King Abdullah II, China-Jordan relations have sustained the momentum of growth, bringing tangible benefits to the two peoples. China will work with Jordan to take the visit as an opportunity to help China-Jordan strategic partnership produce more fruits, and open up new prospects and inject new impetus into growing the bilateral ties. We will release more information on this visit in due course. You are welcome to stay tuned.
In recent years, China-Arab relations enjoy robust development, setting a stellar example of solidarity and cooperation between developing countries. China will work with Arab countries to carry forward traditional friendship, deepen strategic mutual trust, promote mutually beneficial cooperation, and foster closer people-to-people exchanges so as to bring China-Arab relations and cooperation to a new height.
AFP: Sources told AFP and other media outlets that China is weighing a bid to host UN climate talks in 2028. I wonder if you can confirm this or comment on this?

Beijing Daily: Does China have any comment on the Kurultai elections Kazakhstan held yesterday?
Lin Jian: China congratulates Kazakhstan on holding smooth Kurultai elections yesterday. As a friendly neighbor and permanent comprehensive strategic partner, China supports Kazakhstan in independently following a development path befitting its national conditions, and is glad to see sustained security and economic prosperity in the country. We wish Kazakhstan new and greater achievements in national development.
China values its relations with Kazakhstan and stands ready to work with Kazakhstan to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents, deepen all-round mutually beneficial cooperation, and bring the bilateral relations to a new height.
Yonhap News Agency: Today marks the 34th anniversary of ROK-China diplomatic ties. How does China see the significance of this relationship and what are its expectations for bilateral ties going forward?
Lin Jian: Indeed, today marks the 34th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and the ROK. Over the past 34 years, our two countries, as friendly neighbors, have become inseparable strategic cooperative partners with all‑round and rapid growth in politics, economy and trade, people‑to‑people and cultural exchanges. Facts have proven that the development of bilateral relations is in keeping with the trend of the times, serves the shared interests of both countries, and contributes to regional peace and development.
At present, China-ROK relations continue to improve and develop along the direction charted by the two heads of state. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Foreign Minister Wang Yi just paid a visit to the ROK upon invitation, where he had in-depth exchanges with the ROK side on advancing the sound and sustainable development of bilateral ties. China has always placed the ROK high on its agenda for neighborhood diplomacy and stands ready to work with the ROK side to implement the common understandings reached by the two heads of state, bring bilateral strategic cooperative partnership to new heights, and deliver more benefits to the two peoples.
PTI: You just announced the special representative talks between India and China tomorrow. It is a unique, indeed, a very comprehensive mechanism to discuss the overall relations. Maybe you can highlight what are the issues that could be discussed in tomorrow’s talks?
Lin Jian: The Talks Between the Special Representatives of China and India on the Boundary Question are the main channel for negotiations between China and India on the boundary question, and also an important platform for communication between the two sides on issues of mutual interest. In August last year, China and India successfully held the 24th round of talks, during which the two sides had candid and in-depth exchanges of views on the boundary question and reached a number of common understandings. During this round of talks, the two sides will continue the in-depth communication on the boundary question in the spirit of the common understandings between leaders of the two countries to jointly keep the border areas peaceful and tranquil. The two sides will also exchange views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues.
China News Service: We notice that following the UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres’s attendance at the 2026 World AI Conference & High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in China, UN Deputy Secretary-General attended a dialogue on AI and human development in Xi’an. Can you share more details?
Lin Jian: From August 20 to 21, a dialogue on Artificial Intelligence and Human Development was held in Xi’an. The event was co-hosted by China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the UN. UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina J. Mohammed attended and addressed the event. The outcomes of the dialogue will be submitted to the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly.
Not long ago, taking a broader view of social progress, President Xi Jinping shared four observations on the opportunities and challenges brought by AI, stressing the need to adhere to the principle of openness and win-win, strengthen risk-awareness, encourage inclusiveness, and advocate solidarity, which are well-received by the international community. The purpose of this event echoes the important statements of President Xi. Representatives from various countries have explored the profound impact of AI on human development through the lenses of history, philosophy and reality.
The attendance of UN Secretary-General and Deputy Secretary-General at international conferences on AI in China fully demonstrates the significance of AI, a cutting-edge technology, for the world, and also reflects that China always supports the UN’s role as the main channel in global AI governance. Xi’an is where the ancient Silk Road begins and where the East meets the West, and embodies the history of mutual learning and harmonious coexistence among civilizations. Such a place can help various parties draw wisdom from the long history, answer the questions of the times brought by AI, and promote the common welfare of all countries.
Participants from various countries noted that in developing AI, it’s important to take a people-centered approach, develop AI for the positive and for good, share the opportunities, and shoulder the responsibilities together. More emphasis should be put on the interests of developing countries and the disadvantaged groups, and AI can be used to empower human development and progress of civilizations.
China will, together with the UN and all countries in the world, make continuous efforts to ensure the open and inclusive development of AI for good and for all so as to better contribute to the common welfare of the international community.
Reuters: The U.S. Treasury Secretary has threatened secondary sanctions against countries that trade or deal with Iran. China has historically been a major buyer of Iranian oil. If the U.S. does impose secondary sanctions tomorrow, what will be the response from China? (Similar question from Bloomberg)
Lin Jian: Sanctions and pressure tactics do no help in resolving issues. They will only lead to escalation that serves no one’s interest. China calls on parties to act rationally and with restraint, and avoid taking any measure that may further escalate tensions or deal a blow to global economic growth and financial stability. They need to return to the right track of political settlement through dialogue and negotiation at an early date. China will closely watch relevant developments and do what is necessary to protect our legitimate rights and interests.
Global Times: A U.S. official in a recent social media post alleged that high‑risk technologies from Chinese tech companies create risks of espionage, cyber‑attacks, and network disruptions, urging U.S. partners across the Western hemisphere to rapidly shift to reliable supply vendors to protect their citizens and sovereignty. Would you like to comment on this?
Lin Jian: The allegations, full of fact-distorting fabrications, are means of blatant tech‑bullying and unilateral coercion. China firmly rejects them.
Chinese tech firms have become well-known for their advanced technologies, competitive pricing and secure and efficient services. When operating overseas, they strictly abide by local laws, regulations and industry norms. In fact, they have won wide recognition and appreciation from local partners and communities, contributed to host‑country socioeconomic growth and job creation, and proven themselves genuinely reliable suppliers. In stark contrast, the U.S. has long engaged in tapping, surveillance, and cyber-attacks across Latin America and the Caribbean, leaving nations there feeling insecure and distrustful of Washington.
We advise the U.S. to stop its political manipulation, stop interfering with sovereign nations’ right to independently choose cooperation partners, and instead contribute to prosperity and stability in Latin America and the Caribbean through concrete actions.
Beijing Youth Daily: Concerning the case that Hong Kong’s High Court convicted the “Hong Kong Alliance” and its former leaders Lee Cheuk-yan, Ho Chun-yan and Chow Hang-tung of inciting subversion, the EU and certain countries including the U.S. have expressed their concerns in their statements and remarks. What’s China’s response?
Lin Jian: Certain countries and institutions used the judicial case to make malicious smears against Hong Kong and its rule of law, and interfered in China’s internal affair. China firmly opposes it and has lodged serious protests.
The platform of “Hong Kong Alliance” is aimed at subverting state power at its core. The facts concerning the defendants’ crimes are clear and the offense has caused serious harm. It’s legitimate and lawful for the government of Hong Kong SAR to combat the activities endangering national security. Hong Kong upholds rule of law. The central government firmly supports the Hong Kong SAR in safeguarding national security and combating activities that endanger national security in accordance with the law.
Hong Kong affairs are purely China’s internal affairs. We urge relevant parties to earnestly respect China’s sovereignty and the rule of law in Hong Kong, and stop the political manipulation and interference in the Hong Kong affairs and China’s internal affairs in any form.
Bloomberg: I would like to ask about the meeting that Vice Foreign Minister Miao Deyu had with Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi in Beijing. Does the ministry have any more details on that meeting?
Lin Jian: China has shared details about the meeting in a readout, which you may refer to. I have nothing to add. China is closely following the situation in the Middle East and Gulf region and has been actively committed to promoting talks for peace. We stand ready to act in the spirit of the four propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping on safeguarding and promoting peace and stability in the Middle East and make continued effort to help restore peace and tranquility to the Middle East at an early date.
Antara: Another question about the China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism. In the past, Indonesia and China had the High-Level Dialogue Cooperation Mechanism, which led to flagship projects such as the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway. Now China and Indonesia held the China-Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue Mechanism. Are there any joint projects similar to the high-speed railway that are expected to become the result from this newly established dialogue mechanism?
Lin Jian: The China‑Indonesia Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue is an important joint measure implementing the consensus between the two heads of state. It aims to deepen practical cooperation across the fields, advance the building of a community with a shared future, and deliver tangible benefits to both peoples. The Jakarta‑Bandung High‑Speed Railway has served over 16 million passengers with safe and smooth operation since its opening. It has improved local transport conditions and made travel easier for residents along the route, and continues to provide momentum for Indonesia’s economic and social development and regional connectivity. China stands ready to work with Indonesia to make full use of the Comprehensive Strategic Dialogue mechanism, advance high‑quality Belt and Road cooperation, produce more cooperation outcomes in infrastructure and other fields, and inject fresh impetus into our respective modernization.

Zelenskyy proposes identifying the national shrines of the Ukrainian people and establishing liability for damaging them
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
15:40:14 EEST
21:40:14 KST

Zelenskyy proposes identifying the national shrines of the Ukrainian people and establishing liability for damaging them
Kyiv • UNN
The President proposed granting special status to 23 historical sites and strengthening their protection. Intentional damage would be punishable by\r\nup to 10 years in prison.
On Independence Day, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy submitted two bills to the Verkhovna Rada aimed at introducing special legal protection for the national shrines of the Ukrainian people, as well as establishing liability for damaging them. UNN reports this, citing bills Nos. 15550 and №15551.
Details
Bill No. 15550, "On the Protection of the National Shrines of the Ukrainian People," proposes defining the concept of a "National Shrine of the Ukrainian People" as a cultural heritage monument of national significance and/or a World Heritage site that has universal value for the Ukrainian people and exceptional cultural, historical, scientific, or religious significance for the formation and consolidation of the Ukrainian people and the statehood of Ukraine.
The document provides for adding 23 sites to the list of national shrines:
-  Saint Sophia of Kyiv (Saint Sophia Cathedral), Kyiv; 
-  Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra (Ensemble of the Kyiv-Pechersk Lavra), Kyiv; 
-  Chersonesus Taurica (Ruins of the city of Chersonesus), Sevastopol (Crimea); 
-  Pochaiv Lavra (Complex of Buildings of the Pochaiv Holy Dormition Lavra), Pochaiv (Ternopil region); 
-  St. George's Cathedral (St. George's Cathedral), Lviv; 
-  Monk's Mountain (Grave of the poet T. H. Shevchenko), Kaniv (Cherkasy region); 
-  Khan's Palace and the Great Mosque (Khan's Palace Complex), Bakhchysarai (Crimea); 
-  Dormition Cathedral (Foundations of the Cathedral of the Dormition of the Blessed Virgin Mary), the village of Krylos (Ivano-Frankivsk region); 
-  Transfiguration Cathedral, Chernihiv; 
-  Sviatohirsk Lavra (Sviatohirsk Holy Dormition Monastery), Sviatohirsk (Donetsk region); 
-  Residence of the Metropolitans of Bukovina and Dalmatia, Chernivtsi; 
-  Lubart's Castle (Castle), Lutsk (Volyn region); 
-  Kamianets-Podilskyi Fortress (Fortifications of the City), Kamianets-Podilskyi (Khmelnytskyi region); 
-  Khotyn Fortress (Complex of Buildings of Khotyn Fortress), Khotyn (Chernivtsi region); 
-  Akkerman Fortress, Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi (Odesa region); 
-  Carmelite Monastery, Berdychiv (Zhytomyr region); 
-  Palanok Castle, Mukachevo (Zakarpattia region); 
-  St. Elias Church (Church of St. Elias with a Bell Tower), the village of Subotiv (Cherkasy region); 
-  Skovoroda Estate (Memorial Complex of the philosopher and poet H. S. Skovoroda), the village of Skovorodynivka (Kharkiv region); 
-  Citadel of the Baturyn Fortress and Hetman's Palace (Detinets Settlement "Lithuanian Castle" and the Palace of K. H. Razumovsky), Baturyn (Chernihiv region); 
-  Kholodnyi Yar, the village of Melnyky (Cherkasy region); 
-  Zaporizhian Sich on Khortytsia (Historical and Cultural Complex "Zaporizhian Sich"), Zaporizhzhia; 
-  Site of the Battle of Kruty, the village of Pam yatne (Chernihiv region). 
The draft law stipulates that a national shrine is subject to special protection and safeguarding.
For inclusion on the list, a cultural heritage site must have the status of a cultural heritage monument of national significance and/or a World Heritage site and meet at least two of the following criteria:
-  the age of the cultural heritage site exceeds 1,000 years;  
-  be a prominent and unique site of the historical memory of the Ukrainian people, their spirituality and culture, the formation of the Ukrainian people and the statehood of Ukraine, and the consolidation of Ukrainian national and civic identity;  
-  possess characteristics of unique and irreplaceable value to the Ukrainian people;  
-  be directly connected with prominent historical, cultural, religious, military-political, or other important state-building events, and with the lives and activities of prominent individuals who played an important role in such events and made a significant contribution to the development of Ukrainian statehood, its spirituality, culture, science, education, and other spheres of social relations.  
A national shrine may be used for activities aimed at:
-  forming and preserving the national memory of the Ukrainian people; 
-  promoting historical, archaeological, cultural, religious, architectural, scientific, and educational heritage of global and national significance; fostering civic resilience, civic-patriotic, and spiritual and moral education;  
-  cultural, scientific, educational, and religious life;  
-  the holding of ceremonies during state holidays, state celebrations, other important public events, and ceremonial and protocol events attended by senior state officials and high-ranking officials, representatives of foreign states and international organizations;  
-  initiations and the taking of an oath;  
-  the performance of a military funeral ritual;  
-  the implementation of spiritual and psychological recovery programs for servicemen, military chaplains, members of their families, as well as persons discharged from military service who are war veterans or persons with special merits to the Motherland.  
The following list of national sanctities will be determined by the Council on National Sanctities, which is established by the President and will operate as an advisory and consultative body.
Draft Law No. 15551 "On Amendments to the Criminal Code of Ukraine Regarding Strengthening Liability for Crimes Against the National Sanctities of the Ukrainian People" establishes liability for damage to national sanctities.
Thus, the unlawful conduct of archaeological reconnaissance, excavations, and other land or underwater works at an archaeological heritage site will carry a fine of UAH 17,000 to UAH 51,000, or probation supervision for a term of up to two years, or restriction of liberty for the same term, with deprivation of the right to hold certain positions or engage in certain activities for a term of up to three years or without such deprivation.
For the intentional unlawful destruction, demolition, or damage of sites committed against the national sanctities of the Ukrainian people — imprisonment for a term of three to ten years, with deprivation of the right to hold certain positions or engage in certain activities for a term of up to three years or without such deprivation.
In addition, Draft Law No. 15550 also establishes penalties for legal entities for violations of legislation on the protection of cultural heritage; in particular, for conducting any unlawful works that may cause or have caused damage to a national sanctity, a fine of UAH 850,000 to UAH 1.7 million will be imposed.
It should be noted that both documents have been designated by the President as urgent.
To remind you
On August 15, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed Decree No. 726/2026 "On the National Sanctities of the Ukrainian People," which provides for the creation of a separate status for unique sites of Ukraine’s historical, spiritual, and cultural heritage.

Ultra-Orthodox protesters threaten traffic chaos in central Israel during evening rush-hour
Demonstrators plan to block major roads near Bnei Brak on Monday following the arrest of a yeshiva student accused of draft evasion
Ultra-Orthodox protesters are planning to significantly disrupt traffic in central Israel on Monday afternoon over the arrest of a yeshiva student accused of evading the military draft, Israeli media N12 reported.
The demonstration is expected to begin at around 5 pm, likely on Route 4 also known as Geha Road, or Jabotinsky Street, two major roads near Bnei Brak. Similar protests have previously blocked traffic for approximately two and a half hours.
The protest follows the arrest of Israel Gohafi, a student at the Beit Midrash Elyon yeshiva in Bnei Brak who had recently begun studying at a yeshiva in Kfar Hasidim.
Police reportedly stopped Gohafi in Haifa over an issue involving payment for his Rav-Kav public transportation card. Officers then discovered that he was wanted for failing to report for military service and transferred him to the Military Police.
Am Kadosh, an organization that assists those who refuse to enlist, claimed that Gohafi had been “abducted” and taken to a military prison.
The demonstration is being organized by the Hatzafnikim, followers of Rabbi Tzvi Friedman, who have pledged to take to the streets whenever an ultra-Orthodox yeshiva student is arrested for failing to report for military service.
The group confirmed that a protest will take place Monday but has not officially announced its location. Police are nevertheless preparing for major traffic disruptions on roads surrounding Bnei Brak.

Digital financial inclusion key to boosting women's participation in India’s platform economy: ILO-NCAER
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:38:53 UTC
21:38:53 KST

Digital financial inclusion key to boosting women's participation in India’s platform economy: ILO-NCAER
Aug 24, 2026, 18:08 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
NITI Aayog estimates India’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30.
NEW DELHI: Despite the flexibility offered by platform work, women’s participation in India’s growing platform economy remains constrained by limited access to formal financial services, gaps in digital literacy, safety concerns and restrictive social norms, an ILO-NCAER policy brief said on Monday.The brief, “Advancing Women’s Digital Financial Inclusion in the Platform Economy”, said women need access to a range of financial services throughout their platform-work journey, including start-up capital, short-term credit, insurance, savings and financial planning tools.It highlighted cashflow-based lending as a key lever for inclusion, particularly because women are less likely to own land or property that can be used as collateral. Digital records of platform payments can provide lenders with verifiable evidence of income and repayment capacity.Addressing a Roundtable at the release of the Policy Brief, NCAER director general Suresh Goyal said, “A woman’s best protection is a little money of her own and access to credit and mobility are important conditions for women to have better employment opportunities. Platform economy has given that opportunity.”
The brief identified two ways to leverage women’s digital footprints: using India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including the Account Aggregator framework, to make financial data portable, and enabling platforms to partner with lenders to offer loans, savings and insurance through their apps.ILO country director Michiko Miyamoto said, “Digital financial inclusion must enable women to build income security, resilience, and sustainable livelihoods."ILO Senior Specialist Radhicka Kapoor said integrating financial DPI with e-Shram records could further expand access, provided safeguards against algorithmic bias are built in.The brief also flagged device ownership as a barrier, noting that women’s digital access is often mediated through family members.
NITI Aayog estimates India’s platform workforce could rise from 12 million in 2024-25 to 23.5 million by 2029-30.Director of NCAER’s Centre for Gender and Macroeconomy, Prof. Ratna Sahay, summed up the key takeaway, “Digital footprint in platform economies can be a game-changer for women to access credit, underpinned by regulation that encourages innovation while ensuring consumer protection and financial stability.”

Backlash After Hakeem Jeffries Holds Private Meeting With Jared Kushner Ahead of Midterms
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:33:51 UTC
21:33:51 KST

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries met privately with President Donald Trump’s son-in-law and adviser Jared Kushner in recent weeks, prompting criticism from some Democrats ahead of approaching midterm elections, according to reports.
Although Kushner, who served as a senior West Wing adviser during Trump’s first term, does not have a formal role in the current Administration, he has remained involved in Trump’s diplomatic efforts in the Middle East and Russia.
During the meeting, the pair were said to have discussed housing, immigration, and the high cost of living as potential areas of common ground.
The report comes less than three months before the November midterms, when Democrats are favored to retake control of the House from Republicans, who currently hold both chambers of Congress. A Democratic victory would put Jeffries in line to become speaker and give the party greater oversight powers to investigate the Trump Administration.
The meeting—an unusual instance of a top Democrat and a Trump confidant coming together to discuss potential areas of agreement—has drawn scrutiny from some within Democratic circles.
TIME has reached out to the White House and the offices of Kushner and Jeffries for comment. It was first reported Sunday by the New York Times and has since been confirmed by multiple outlets.
Asked whether he supported the meeting during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday, Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said: “I’m in favor of people meeting with whoever they want to discuss ideas. But it’s one thing to have a meeting. It’s another thing to see something real come out of that.”
Tommy Vietor, a former aide to President Barack Obama and now a co-host of the podcast Pod Save America, was far less diplomatic.
“Jared Kushner has no actual government job, he just uses his family connections to get money from Gulf autocrats and fund corrupt deals. The only way Jeffries should work with him is with demands for documents and subpoenas,” Vietor said.
House Speaker Mike Johnson said Sunday that he first learned of the meeting that same day, when reports began circulating in the media.
"I don't know what that's about," Johnson said on Fox News. "I know Jared has interests and lots of other things going on. He's not really directly involved in the admin, at least in the day-to-day in the White House."
Johnson, however, remained confident that Republicans could retain control of the House.
“I’m telling you what, you better not bet against the House Republicans,” he said.
Trump has met with the top Democratic leaders of the House and Senate only once since returning to office, when the President attempted last year to reach an agreement to prevent a government shutdown. Those talks ultimately failed, leading to the longest government shutdown in U.S. history.
The relationship between Trump, Jeffries, and other members of the Democratic leadership has often been marked by conflict and back-and-forth name-calling.
In late April, Trump called Jeffries a “low IQ person” and attacked Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer over their opposition to the Iran war, branding them “traitor Democrats.”
Jeffries, in turn, called Trump the “dumbest President ever” in response to the President’s insults during a press conference.
Trump has continued to attack the top House Democrat as "low IQ" and a "thug” branding him as a “danger” to the country.
More recently, however, Trump’s tone toward Jeffries appears to have softened. In an interview earlier this month with Punchbowl News, the President said he could work with the Democratic leader and described him as a "nice guy."
"People are harsh on me. I'm harsh on them. It's part of the world," Trump said. "I'd probably get along with him very well."
Since returning to the White House, Trump has often sought to bypass Congress and pursue policy through executive action, from curbing birthright citizenship to the implementation of tariffs.
That dynamic could change if Democrats take control of the House, where Republicans currently hold a slim majority of 218 Republicans to 212 Democrats and one independent.
A Democratic-controlled House would give the party the power to block parts of Trump’s legislative agenda, launch high-profile congressional investigations, issue subpoenas, and initiate impeachment proceedings.
Trump—who was impeached twice during his first term—has urged voters to back Republicans in the midterms, arguing that Democrats would use their power to impeach him again.
“I’m going to be impeached. They're going to impeach me. They have no idea why,” he told a crowd during a rally in South Carolina last Friday.
The latest Emerson College polling, released August 20, found congressional Democrats leading Republicans by nearly 8 points. A separate Reuters/Ipsos poll released Aug. 17 found Democrats ahead by 5 points. All 435 House seats are up for election in November.

Brussels witnessed two more shootings last night

There were two more shootings in Brussels last night. Around midnight, the police found a man on the street in the borough of Molenbeek. He had been hit by a bullet in his lower leg. Around 3 am, one person was injured in a shooting in the borough of Sint-Gilles. Jurgen De Landsheer, head of the Brussels South police zone, believes the situation is deteriorating once again. “We need to get the people off the streets who are being exploited by gangs and who are shooting at buildings or people for a few hundred euros.”
In the two new incidents in Sint-Jans-Molenbeek and Sint-Gillis last night, one person was injured in each case. The victims were taken to hospital.
Following the shooting in Sint-Gillis, two suspects were arrested in the neighbourhood. The police cannot yet say whether this is drug-related violence. “The investigation is in full swing. No further details can be provided at this stage,” they said.
There were also several shootings in Brussels last weekend. In Anderlecht, shots were fired at a police station on multiple occasions. There were also two shooting incidents in Sint-Gillis.
‘It was actually a relatively quiet summer,’ says Jurgen De Landsheer. He works in the Brussels South Police Zone, which also includes Anderlecht and Saint-Gillis. "We maintained a fair amount of control over the neighbourhoods, partly because the police continued to apply pressure, and partly through prevention. Now, however, there seems to be a return of the instability."
“It may sound strange to say this is a positive thing, but the renewed violence does show that we are putting pressure on these gangs and disrupting their activities,” says De Landsheer.
Jean Spinette, Mayor of Saint-Gillis, linked last weekend’s shootings to violence between drug gangs. Sooner or later, innocent people will be killed, he said.
Like Spinette, Chief Constable De Landsheer is convinced that last weekend’s shootings are linked to violence between drug gangs. We must continue to focus on law enforcement and prevention, he says.
“I know I’m repeating myself, but on the one hand we must remove drugs and violence from our streets, whilst on the other hand something must take their place,” says De Landsheer. “We must take a positive approach, and that positive narrative is shaped by the community itself.”
The police chief points out that drug gangs target vulnerable people who are easily persuaded to get involved. “I’m talking, for example, about minors and people living here illegally, who hang around on the streets with nothing to do. They are, in effect, being used by the drug gangs as cheap labour.”
“First and foremost, we must focus on robust enforcement, but we must also get the people off the streets who are being exploited by the gangs and who, for a few hundred euros, shoot at or intimidate buildings or people. It is not the major gang leaders who do this.”
“These guys need a swift decision on their status in Belgium so we can get them off the streets, either by integrating them successfully or by sending them back to their country of origin.”
‘Not just a story about the police and the justice system’
This is not only a story about the police and the justice system, emphasises De Landsheer. ‘As a society, we are really going to have to make choices and decide where we want to go with certain issues.’
‘These are issues that must be tackled collectively. The solutions also lie within the neighbourhoods themselves. They must work together with the government, the police, the justice system and other services to give these young people a future. So that they do not feel the need to turn to the world of drugs for easy money.’
De Landsheer describes the shooting at the police station in Anderlecht as a line that has been crossed. “A police station must be a safe place for everyone – for members of the public who come to the station, but also for our own officers.”
De Landsheer realises that there is “no magic solution”. “I don’t think it will stop just like that; we’re seeing the same thing in other cities. But we’re not going to abandon the terrain; we’re going to keep going and try to resolve this together with other services.”

China’s view of Trump’s America has changed from alarm to a shrug
Erratic and transactional, the US leader’s approach exposes domestic governance flaws and the limits of Washington’s containment strategy
3-MIN READ3-MIN
1
 Listen
Wang Wen is a professor and executive dean of the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies, Renmin University of China. 
There is no shortage of Western commentary on US President Donald Trump’s second term. What’s missing is an honest account of how 1.4 billion of us in China see it – or at least how China’s officials and scholars do, since that’s who I can speak for here. I’ve spent a decade watching that view change, from real alarm in 2017 to something closer to a shrug today.
Four things now count as consensus among Chinese scholars. One, Trump is undermining America’s alliance system. His first term rattled Washington’s furniture. His second is dismantling the house. He has purged the civil service, stretched executive power, taxed friend and foe alike, and gutted America’s contribution to global public goods.
He appears to be governing for the next election, not the next generation – and this is speeding up the arrival of a multipolar world.
Two, hostility to China is bipartisan in Washington, but Trump’s version comes with a price tag, which we find oddly reassuring. When tariffs on Chinese goods hit 145 per cent last year, American retailers, farmers and manufacturers howled, inflation bit and the White House backed into a truce. The lesson we draw: his toughness is a negotiating tactic, not a crusade. That leaves room to manage the relationship.
Three, pressure has been a poor substitute for actual containment. The 2018 trade war spooked Chinese firms. By 2026, the mood has flipped. Turns out sanctions are quite good at building the thing they’re meant to prevent.
Chinese chipmakers have scaled up mature 28-nanometre production. Home-grown chip-design software now holds a quarter of the domestic market. Solar panels and electric vehicles have found new buyers across Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Latin America. America’s share of China’s trade shrank.

In Russia, temporary administration has been authorized for critical infrastructure facilities if they have not been secured against air attacks
Kyiv • UNN
Putin's decree allows the Russian authorities to take over the management of critical facilities due to security threats or delays in restoration. This concerns energy, industry, communications, and essential services.
Russian dictator Vladimir Putin has allowed the introduction of “temporary administration” at infrastructure facilities whose owners fail to ensure their security. This is stated in a decree on “measures to ensure the security of critical infrastructure facilities,” UNN reports, citing Russian media.
Details
According to Putin’s decree, the authorities will be able to introduce temporary administration at infrastructure facilities whose owners “fail to take security measures” in “conditions of external threats.”
Temporary administration may also be introduced when the restoration of such facilities is delayed.
This concerns, in particular, fuel and energy sector facilities, industrial facilities, life-support facilities, nuclear power facilities, and communications.

Museum heists have turned more violent, with thieves hired on social media, Europol says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:28:33 UTC
21:28:33 KST

Museum heists have turned more violent, with thieves hired on social media, Europol says
BRUSSELS, Aug 24 - Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies focusing on gold and jewels, and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad-hoc opportunists recruited through social media, Europol said on Monday.
The heist at the Louvre Museum in Paris in October last year was a prime example of these shifts, Europol said, as the thieves threatened guards and visitors, and stole €88 million worth of jewels such as Empress Eugenie's tiara.
Over the last two years, art thieves have shifted their attention to precious metals, jewels and cultural artefacts that offer greater profits, the EU's law enforcement agency said in a report.
The price of gold has surged 85% over the past two years, as investors and central banks turn to the metal as a safe haven. The London Bullion Market Association, which oversees London's over-the-counter gold trading hub, has warned that "as gold prices rise to historic levels, illicit flows and market distortions are also increasing."
Europol said: "offenders are breaching premises and display cases using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives."
Where traditional gangs used "deception and stealth", had a central leader and niche expertise, recent thefts were carried out by a decentralised ad-hoc group of profit-seeking opportunists, recruited through social media on a "crime-as-a-service" basis, it said.
Europol added thieves were increasingly targeting gold items from nuggets and coins to jewels.
"Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process. Precious stones in jewellery, on the other hand, can be easily removed and sold further," the report said.
In January last year, thieves used explosives to steal a 2,500-year-old Dacian golden helmet and three ancient gold bracelets from a museum in the Netherlands. The artefacts were later recovered and returned to Romania, although one bracelet is still missing.
Europol also noted an increase in thefts of ancient Chinese porcelain artefacts such as Ming Dynasty vases due to high demand. REUTERS

South Korea says the United States has cancelled a large joint amphibious landing exercise scheduled for next month due to constraints on force availability caused by the US-Israel war on Iran.
“The US Marine Corps formally notified our forces in June that its ability to deploy forces during this year’s Ssangyong exercise would be constrained due to the situation in the Middle East,” Han Seung-jeon, a spokesman for the South Korean Marine Corps, told reporters at a news briefing on Monday.

The biennial Ssangyong drills involve marine forces from South Korea and the US and are designed to strengthen combined operations, typically involving warships, aircraft and ground forces rehearsing amphibious landings.
Seoul and Washington were continuing consultations on resuming the amphibious exercise, the spokesman said, without giving details.

Despite the reduction of the exercises, North Korea fired 10 short-range ballistic missiles last week and issued a statement denouncing the drills.
North Korea has long condemned such joint exercises as rehearsals for invasion.
The US president also said last week that it was important to “get along” with Kim, adding that Pyongyang now had 57 “very powerful” nuclear weapons. Seoul estimates that North Korea has 80 to 120 such weapons.
Trump met Kim three times during his first term, but Pyongyang accelerated its nuclear programmes after their second summit in Hanoi in 2019 collapsed without an agreement on North Korea’s denuclearisation.

Russian military reveals man-portable laser gun (VIDEO)
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:26:27 UTC
21:26:27 KST

Russian military reveals man-portable laser gun (VIDEO)
The Russian military has showcased a new man-portable laser system designed to safely disable mines and unexploded ordnance from up to 100 meters away.
The gun featured in a report by the military’s official media outlet, Zvezda TV, on Sunday is derived from a larger system designed for remotely controlled small ground vehicles. The channel demonstrated both variants alongside other modules intended for the tracked Kurier (“courier”) platform, which is being widely adopted by the Russian military.
The smaller gun is powered by a backpack-style battery pack and features a 1-kilowatt laser. Its beam is strong enough to burn through a plastic casing within seconds, provided the operator maintains a steady aim. The video showed that the best results are achieved when the weapon is mounted on a tripod.
The larger variant has twice the power and places the projector on a retractable lifting platform, allowing the laser to be fired from behind cover. Its greater stability and beam strength give it a range of up to 500 meters, according to the developer. Both the rover-mounted module and the man-portable gun have entered serial production.
A laser bomb-disposal system works by igniting the high explosives inside the targeted munition and burning them without causing a detonation. Operating from a distance is necessary in high-risk environments and helps reduce the danger posed by booby traps equipped with advanced sensors that may be triggered when a bomb-disposal specialist or conventional robot approaches.
The Zvezda report also demonstrated other modules developed for the Kurier platform, including some designed by a frontline engineering unit involved in the Ukraine conflict. One of its creations is fitted with a drill and is used to prepare holes for poles before anti-drone nets are installed over roads in the battle zone.
Both Russia and Ukraine are developing new uses for remotely operated vehicles, which are increasingly being deployed for combat, resupply, medical evacuation, and military engineering missions.

Yordan Alvarez’s Triple Crown bid will have to survive a major challenge from the AL East
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-24
12:23:01 UTC
21:23:01 KST

Yordan Alvarez’s Triple Crown bid will have to survive a major challenge from the AL East
As the season winds down, Houston slugger Yordan Alvarez will have to worry about two sets of spoilers.
The first is the more traditional type — teams that will try to beat the Astros in key games and deny them a spot in the postseason.
The other includes individual spoilers — players who could prevent Alvarez from making history as baseball’s next Triple Crown winner.
Alvarez currently leads the American League with a .320 average, 36 home runs and 90 RBIs. If he holds onto the top spot in all three categories, he’d be the first batter to win the Triple Crown since Miguel Cabrera in 2012. The biggest threats Alvarez faces all come from the AL East.
The next-highest batting averages in the AL both belong to Tampa Bay players — Chandler Simpson at .310 and Yandy Díaz at .306. Fortunately for Alvarez, there aren’t any stealth candidates — players with high averages who don’t currently have enough plate appearances to qualify, but would by the end of the season.
The home run race is currently the tightest, with Tampa Bay’s Junior Caminero just one behind with 35. Ben Rice of the New York Yankees has 34. There are times when Alvarez seems like Houston’s only major threat offensively, and he’s been intentionally walked 28 times — way more than Caminero (10) and Rice (four). Those lost opportunities could matter in a close race.
Alvarez’s closest competition in RBIs is Baltimore’s Pete Alonso, who has 85. Alonso recently went on a 14-game hitting streak. Caminero is also in the mix with 83 RBIs.
When Cabrera pulled off the Triple Crown in 2012, he had to hold off Hall of Famers Joe Mauer and Adrian Beltre in batting average, as well as likely Hall of Famer Mike Trout. He finished one homer ahead of Josh Hamilton and Curtis Granderson.
Trivia time
Alvarez broke Jeff Bagwell’s franchise record for intentional walks in a season. Bagwell drew 27 in 1997. Who is in third place on that list for Houston?
Performance of the week
Pete Crow-Armstrong hit a leadoff homer in the bottom of the first and a walk-off shot in the 10th to give the Chicago Cubs a 7-5 win over the White Sox on Monday night.
The Cubs then won in walk-off fashion again a night later against the White Sox, but were beaten via the walk-off twice in a row by Seattle later in the week. The Cubs have 13 walk-off wins this year, the most in baseball, but the White Sox and Mariners aren’t far behind with 11.
Comeback of the week
Philadelphia was down 4-0 with two outs in the bottom of the ninth Sunday before rallying for a 6-4 victory over St. Louis. Edmundo Sosa hit a three-run double, and Bryan De La Cruz hit a single that tied the game. Then Kyle Schwarber won it with his major league-leading 39th homer of the season.
It was the ninth straight victory for the Phillies, who now trail first-place Atlanta by only three games in the NL East. The Braves were 9 1/2 games up less than two weeks ago.
It’s been a bizarre season for Philadelphia, which was 8-18 by late April, then went 48-27, then lost eight of its last games in July before going 16-5 so far in August.
Team of the week
Kansas City was the lone team to go 7-0 over the past week, although the Phillies and Los Angeles Dodgers both went 6-0. The Royals took advantage of four games against the dreadful Athletics before sweeping three in a row from a Detroit team that’s chasing a playoff berth.
Last-place Kansas City is actually 36-30 at home this year but has gone 22-44 on the road.
Trivia answer
Rusty Staub drew 24 intentional walks for the Astros in 1968.

JOHANNESBURG (AP) — Four suspects in the killing of former world champion boxer Zolani Tete were arrested, South African police said Monday.
Tete was in his car outside his home last week when men wearing balaclavas opened fire, police said. A woman who was in the vehicle was injured and has since been hospitalized.
The shooting took place at Mdantsane, Eastern Cape, according to the police. Tete was arriving at his residence and waiting for the gate to open when he was ambushed by two armed suspects.
Police said one of the suspects arrested two days ago was expected to appear in court on Monday, while the other three would appear on a later date.
Tete held the World Boxing Federation flyweight title from 2007 to 2008 and the World Boxing Organization bantamweight title in 2017 and 2019.

AP Decision Notes: What to expect in Georgia’s special congressional runoff
